pass: PREUAT2-1 defect-follower #3 (implementer half of the fix-first protocol; restore readiness after the VIEW intent)

defect.caughtOn: S25+ live demo, this hour: the credential card flow worked end-to-end (owner typed the secret on the masked card twice, the approval carried — [credential-redacted] everywhere, the redaction law proven live), the restore fired with the normalized URL — but the injection 'execute: type ... -> FAILED' BOTH times
defect.summary: The fixed 1000ms Config.restoreSettleMs expired before Chrome was actually front+interactive on Samsung OneUI (the activity resume + VIEW-intent page restore take longer), so the focus-first tap landed wrong and the gesture failed; the subsequent observation then read the wrong window and the run starved to REFUSED.

fix.mechanism: After restoreBrowserForeground fires the VIEW intent it now WAITS FOR OBSERVATION READINESS before the step continues: waitForBrowserReadiness() re-observes on the existing unusable-tree cadence (Config.unusableRetryDelayMs) until a read passes the loop's own usable-tree bar (non-empty lines >= minUsableNodes + pageNodes >= minPageNodes), bounded by the new Config.restoreReadinessMs (default 10s -> ~6 retries + the initial probe). The wait rides BOTH call sites (gate card and completion card) because it lives inside restoreBrowserForeground, right after the settle; the loud no-URL path (no intent fired) waits for nothing; overlay/never-fronting/trusted/task-ending exclusions are untouched. On budget expiry the step proceeds anyway — the next observe's own starvation machinery (refuseAfterUnusableReads) owns a still-dark page; no new failure mode. Outcome logged loudly: 'restore: browser ready after Nms' / 'restore: browser not readable within budget - continuing'. Config.restoreSettleMs stays as the pre-observe initial settle, default raised 1000 -> 2000 (dispatch-sanctioned, ART-5: Config; the old value wasted the first re-read on OneUI). The readiness probes are wall-clock WITHIN the same step (same precedent as restoreSettleMs): they consume no budget and no steps, and the step's enumerate/decide/execute state is unchanged — the probes only gate WHEN the step continues. Seam shape kept: restoreBrowserForeground is still the loop-local suspend fun; waitForBrowserReadiness is a loop-local suspend fun using the loop's own observer/usable/notePageUrl/line/clock. notePageUrl is called on the probes (they are observations).

deviations: The readiness budget is enforced as a re-read count derived from Config.restoreReadinessMs / Config.unusableRetryDelayMs (~10s at the defaults) rather than a clock check — the loop's Clock is fakeable and static in JVM tests, so a clock-only bound would either hang tests or need a second backstop; the count bound is deterministic in tests and ~wall-clock-identical in production (each retry sleeps the cadence). restoreReadinessMs=0 means one probe, no retries (the timeout test uses this).
restoreSettleMs default raised 1000 -> 2000 (explicitly offered by the dispatch; judged helpful — OneUI's resume+restore outlasted 1000ms, so the first re-read was wasted)
